title: The visual gate captures components but not patterns, so a pattern can break unseen
foundBy: user report (repository owner): "a couple of things broke on the Explorer pattern", after the Tree work in CUI-008

evidence.verified: npm run visual:capture: 35 components, 9 patterns and 3 interaction states per theme, taking the gate from 76 screenshots to 94. Two consecutive compares both reported 94/94 with 0 differing pixels, so the pattern captures are deterministic. Reapplying the Tree flex regression fails the run by name: FAIL light/pattern-explorer.png at 1034 pixels and FAIL dark at 1050. npm run check exit 0, axe violations 0 in both themes.

details:
`visual:capture` records 35 components and 3 interaction states per theme. It records no patterns. A pattern composes several components, which is exactly where a change that is right for one component in isolation goes wrong, and nothing looks at them.

This is not theoretical. A `flex: 1 1 auto` added to Tree's label for CUI-008 made the label fill its row. In a flipped tree, which lays its row out with `row-reverse`, that pinned every label to the far edge instead of beside its icon. The label measured 231px wide at an 8px gap from the row's left edge, where it should have been 20px wide at a 219px gap. `visual:compare` passed 76 of 76 screenshots throughout, because the Explorer pattern is not among them. The repository owner found it by opening the page.

The capture list is also fixed rather than derived: it stayed at 35 components while the catalog went to 37, so the Tooltip added in CUI-016 is not captured either. A new component joins the gate only if somebody remembers to add it.

Two things worth separating. Adding the nine pattern tabs to the baseline closes most of the hole. Deriving the list from the catalog stops it reopening.

notes.text: Found by sweeping all nine pattern tabs in both themes against a build of main, which is what the gate should have been doing. After fixing the flex, every pattern matched except two that differ for good reasons: the markdown viewer demo prints bundle sizes, which grew from 166,136 to 167,230 bytes, and the agent activity demo captures a streaming cursor mid-animation.
The discipline half is written down: CONTRIBUTING.md now lists patterns as a fifth file that moves with a component, and says plainly that nothing enforces it. This record is the enforcement half.

Closed in two halves. The nine pattern pages are captured with their trees expanded, because a pattern at rest shows collapsed rows and hides the composition. Reduced motion is emulated so the agent activity page stops landing mid-animation, which StreamingText already honours.

The first version of this did not work. It captured the patterns and still passed the regression: 2084 differing pixels spread across a whole-page shot stayed under the 0.1% per-image ratio. A ratio dilutes a real layout shift in a large capture, so an absolute floor of 250 pixels now sits alongside it. That is safe because runs in the pinned image are deterministic to the pixel.

Recapturing removed the preview-only palette lab overlay from 28 existing captures, which had been baked into the baseline. The capture now seeds it closed. Accessibility is unchanged: violations 0 to 0 and incomplete 1 to 1, with passes 53 to 52 because a collapsed overlay leaves one rule no nodes to check.

The list is still explicit rather than derived, because several catalogued components cannot be captured at rest: Tooltip renders only while open, and Chip, Legend, RadioGroup and SegmentedControl have no section of their own. A check now fails when the catalog names a component this file neither captures nor excuses, which is what stops it falling behind again.
